primary_topics: Brief birthday toast by CJP for Archit Bartolome's 74th birthday, June 26, 2015

Structure of deliberate inadequacy: CJP uses the repeated refrain 'My words are inadequate' to frame each achievement category before describing it -- a rhetorical device that amplifies each achievement by first disclaiming the ability to describe it

Archit's achievements across eight domains: UE alumnus distinction, TOYM, banking (PNB), management (MAP), finance (FINEX), civic leadership (Rotary Manila), public service (BCDA), faith (Ligaya ng Panginoon)
sub_topics: Eight domains of inadequacy, each naming a specific achievement: (1) young man -- Most Distinguished Alumnus of University of the East; celebrated TOYM Awardee; (2) banker -- Chairman or President of several banks including Philippine National Bank (then the largest banking institution); (3) manager/executive -- President of Management Association of the Philippines (MAP) and Financial Executives Institute of the Philippines (FINEX); (4) civic leader -- President of Rotary Club of Manila ('the first and, during his term, the largest Rotary Club in Asia'); (5) man of God -- couple-leader of Ligaya ng Panginoon with wife Nenne; (6) public servant -- Presidential Cabinet member; Chairman of the Bases Conversion Development Authority (BCDA); (7) father -- reared 'an outstanding son, and beautiful and talented daughters'; (8) husband -- 'successfully wooed a beautiful, brainy and devoted wife whom he adores and worships day and night'
The deliberate-inadequacy structure: the refrain 'My words are inadequate' repeated eight times, each time preceding a specific achievement -- the inadequacy as the highest praise
Closing: 'Nothing really, except to cheer him up and remind him how lucky he is to be among God's chosen disciples on earth! Happy Birthday Archit!' followed by 'Hep! Hep! Hurray!'

stances.claim: The repeated refrain 'My words are inadequate' is not false modesty but the most effective rhetorical device for a person whose achievements are genuinely superlative -- the disclaimer amplifies what follows by first establishing its own insufficiency. CJP uses it eight consecutive times, each time naming a specific achievement, making the structure itself the tribute.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered June 26, 2015 as a birthday toast for Archit Bartolome's 74th birthday, this brief tribute by CJP is structured entirely around the anaphoric refrain 'My words are inadequate' -- applied eight consecutive times to as many domains: as a young man (Most Distinguished Alumnus of UE; TOYM Awardee); as a banker (Chairman/President of several banks including the PNB when it was the largest banking institution in the country); as a manager and executive (President of both MAP and FINEX); as a civic leader (President of the Rotary Club of Manila -- 'the first and, during his term, the largest Rotary Club in Asia'); as a man of God (couple-leader of Ligaya ng Panginoon with wife Nenne); as a public servant (Presidential Cabinet member; BCDA Chairman); as a father (an outstanding son and beautiful talented daughters); and as a husband ('successfully wooed a beautiful, brainy and devoted wife whom he adores and worships day and night'). CJP concludes: 'Truly, my words are inadequate to describe the many-splendored achievements of Archit. What then can I say about him now on his 74th birthday? Nothing really, except to cheer him up and remind him how lucky he is to be among God's chosen disciples on earth! Happy Birthday Archit! Hep! Hep! Hurray!'
